patterns_data.pattern_details: A meaningful share of the increase sits in authorization code movement and claims classified to Not Mapped facility buckets rather than a clean care-delivery trend. Business action should wait until the authorization-to-claim and facility mapping logic is confirmed.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If these shifts are coding or mapping artifacts, UM, reimbursement, and network actions would target the wrong root cause.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a focused audit of authorization code assignment and facility mapping for the cited states, reconcile whether claims moved into AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION or Not Mapped buckets, and only then route confirmed findings to UM or contracting.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Authorization code distribution and unmapped facility classification may reflect coding or mapping movement rather than true utilization or reimbursement change.

CA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added about +$1.1M, led by electrolyte disorders with MCC at +$696K and sepsis without prolonged ventilation at +$409K.
Facility classified as Not Mapped added about +$417K in GA, +$143K in PA, +$126K in KY, with smaller additional impacts in OH and CA.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Outside the largest markets, authorized inpatient growth is recurring across acute hospital, rehab, and critical access settings. Most of the increase is volume-led, but several markets also show higher paid per admit, especially in KY and smaller mixed-pressure pockets. The pattern is concentrated enough at named providers and facility types to support targeted UM and local network action rather than a broad national response.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Recurring growth across multiple smaller markets can accumulate into a material trend and often reflects local admission management or provider concentration issues.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Prioritize market-by-market reviews for KY, VA, OH, CT, NY, NV, and ME to confirm admission drivers, then target local UM controls and provider discussions where growth is concentrated at specific facilities or providers.
evidence_summary: KY acute hospital PPO Local added about +$497K on 16 more admissions, with roughly +$1.6K paid per admit.
VA growth at MARY WASHINGTON HOSPITAL INC added about +$345K on 25 more admissions.
OH added about +$300K in acute hospital use and another +$264K in Physical Rehab.
CT, GA, and NY acute hospital utilization added about +$443K, with MANCHESTER MEMORIAL HOSPITAL at +$81K and HIGHLAND HOSPITAL at +$72K among notable contributors.
